context: After adjusting for age and income, night shift work remained associated with type 2 diabetes (odds ratio 1.42; 95% CI, 1.10 to 1.83; p = 0.007).

reply.answer: The odds ratio of 1.42 compares the odds of type 2 diabetes in night shift workers with other workers, where 1 would mean no difference. The 95% CI of 1.10 to 1.83 sits entirely above 1, and p = 0.007 is the chance of a result this strong if there were no real link. It's still an association after adjusting for age and income, so it doesn't show night shifts cause diabetes.

context: In mice fed a high-fat diet, hepatic steatosis developed within eight weeks, and liver enzymes rose in the blood.

reply.answer: That's fatty liver. When the body takes in more fat than it can burn, the liver stores the extra in its own cells, and stuffed cells leak enzymes, which is why the blood tests went up.
